response: Yes, training at an intensity that feels 'good' can improve physical health. Affect-regulated exercise intensity, which involves exercising at a level that is enjoyable and feels good, can lead to increased motivation, adherence, and overall physical activity. This approach can help individuals stick to their exercise routine, resulting in improved cardiovascular health, weight management, and enhanced mental well-being. Additionally, exercising at a pleasant intensity can reduce stress and anxiety, while also promoting positive emotional states, which can further contribute to overall physical health and well-being.
